findings.text: A truncated feed is detected only after `RunThreads` has rewritten `threads.json`: the refresh writes the partial feed, then `readInputs` checks `resp.Data.Truncated` at line 129, so the `drain-failed` refusal leaves a partial feed where a complete one used to be. Spec §3 says to 'refuse drain-failed before any agent launch or write' and §10 says 'Every refusal comes before the first write.'
findings.quote: resp, ref := fetchcore.RunThreads(ctx, refreshRequest(r, req, fl))

findings.text: Every refusal returned by the threads refresh is rewritten as `drain-failed`, discarding typed codes such as `bad-provider`, `threads-failed` and `canceled` that the shared threads path returns. Spec §7 reserves `drain-failed` for an unreadable bundle or `threads.json`, a truncated feed, or an unreadable login, so an invalid `--provider` or a cancellation mid-refresh reports the wrong code to callers.

`--max-threads` is validated here, after the live refresh (line 64) and the login read (line 132), so an out-of-range value performs host reads and rewrites `threads.json` before the usage refusal. Spec §10 requires every refusal before the first write; the range check belongs in `parseFlags`.

The drafting launcher runs after `drain.json` has already been written at line 93, so a bad `--agent` or `--timeout` refuses only after the plan landed, leaving a plan for a run that never drafted. Spec §10 requires refusals before the first write.

With `--agent` and zero pending threads the agent does not launch and no `drain.replies.json` is written, yet `next` still names `--post`; the spec's draft→`--post` transition assumes drafts exist, and this build has no `--post` flag for the operator to run.
findings.quote: return "post the drafts with verdict drain " + req.Repo + " " + req.Pr + " --post"
